question_text: Outline how paging can let an operating system run a process whose virtual address space is larger than the RAM currently available to it.
adaptation_rationale: Memory management explicit; paging is a concrete example. Scenario and wording rewritten; source reasoning retained only within supported 2027 scope.
solution: Only needed pages are kept in RAM; absent pages can be brought from secondary storage when accessed, replacing other pages if necessary.

marking_points.criterion: Only part of process resident in RAM.
OS moves needed pages between RAM and secondary storage.
